## HEADNOTE
Sample Consumer Protection Act, 2010, Section 3 - warranty - the manufacturer bears the burden of proving that a defect was caused by misuse.
## FACTS
A laptop stopped working within its warranty period. The manufacturer refused service, saying the screen showed signs of liquid damage.
## ARGUMENTS
The manufacturer argued that the consumer must prove the defect was inherent. The consumer argued that the duty under Section 3 is unconditional during the warranty period.
## REASONING
Section 3 places the duty to repair on the manufacturer during the warranty period. Misuse is an exception to that duty and the party relying on an exception must prove it. A bare assertion of liquid damage without an inspection report is not proof.
## HOLDING
The manufacturer must repair or replace the laptop because it did not prove misuse.
